title: 哈姆雷特 4-1~4 放逐英格蘭
style_suffix: black and white ink comic style, high contrast, heavy shadows, cold gothic atmosphere
characters: Hamlet, a lean young prince dressed head to toe in black, a short dark cloak, tousled dark hair, pale clean-shaven face with shadowed sleepless eyes

panels.prompt: Queen Gertrude, a stately middle-aged queen with coiled auburn braids under a golden circlet, in a layered brocade gown, still shaken, reporting to King Claudius, a broad heavyset king with a neatly trimmed dark pointed beard, a wide gold crown, fur-trimmed brocade robes, a jeweled goblet in hand, in a cold grey morning chamber

dialogue.speaker: 葛簇特
dialogue.text: 他瘋得像互相爭勝的大海和狂風。他聽見帷幕後有動靜，拔劍就刺——把那位好老人家殺了。
dialogue.en: Mad as the sea and wind, when both contend which is the mightier: in his lawless fit, behind the arras hearing something stir, whips out his rapier... and... kills the unseen good old man.

panels.prompt: close-up of the king turning away to the window, goblet forgotten, his face all cold calculation with fear underneath

dialogue.speaker: 克勞地
dialogue.text: 要是我在那裡，躺下的就是我。放著他這樣，對誰都是威脅——這件事必須小心處置。
dialogue.en: It had been so with us, had we been there: his liberty is full of threats to all... this vile deed we must, with all our majesty and skill, both countenance and excuse.

panels.prompt: torch-lit corridor at night, Rosencrantz, a plump smooth-faced courtier with a short blond bowl-cut and an eager ingratiating smile, and Guildenstern, a thin courtier with lank dark hair and nervous darting eyes, pressing {characters} with questions, the prince smiling maddeningly

dialogue.speaker: 羅森克蘭茲
dialogue.en: What have you done, my lord, with the dead body?

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 屍體和國王在一起，可是國王沒有和屍體在一起。國王是一件東西——
dialogue.en: The body is with the king, but the king is not with the body. The king is a thing—

panels.prompt: throne room, {characters} standing insolently loose before the enthroned king, guards flanking him

dialogue.speaker: 克勞地
dialogue.text: 哈姆雷特，波隆尼在哪裡？

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 在吃晚飯。不是他在吃，是蛆蟲在吃他——一場政治性的蟲宴。
dialogue.en: At supper... Not where he eats, but where he is eaten: a certain convocation of politic worms are e'en at him.

panels.prompt: {characters} sweeping a mocking farewell bow to the fuming king, guards already gripping the prince's shoulders to march him off

dialogue.speaker: 克勞地
dialogue.en: Therefore prepare thyself... every thing is bent for England.

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 好——去英格蘭！再會，親愛的母親。
dialogue.en: For England! Good. — Farewell, dear mother.

dialogue.speaker: 克勞地
dialogue.text: 是你慈愛的父親，哈姆雷特。

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 父親跟母親是夫妻，夫妻是一體。所以——再會，我的母親。
dialogue.en: My mother: father and mother is man and wife; man and wife is one flesh; and so, my mother.

panels.prompt: King Claudius alone at a high window watching a ship's sails shrink toward the horizon, his reflection ghosted in the glass, one hand crushing a sealed letter

dialogue.speaker: 克勞地
dialogue.text: 英格蘭王啊——照我密函上的指示辦：把哈姆雷特立刻處死。辦好它，英格蘭。
dialogue.en: And, England... thou mayst not coldly set our sovereign process; which imports at full... the present death of Hamlet. Do it, England.

quote.text: 把哈姆雷特立刻處死。辦好它，英格蘭
quote.en: The present death of Hamlet. Do it, England.

panels.prompt: a bleak coastal plain under a huge grey sky, an army column with pikes and banners crossing tiny in the far distance like a line of ants, {characters} halted in the foreground with two guards, watching them pass

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 兩萬個人，為了一塊還不夠埋葬他們的土地，像上床一樣走向墳墓。而我呢——父親被害、母親受辱，理由比天大，卻讓一切沉睡。
dialogue.en: The imminent death of twenty thousand men, that, for a fantasy and trick of fame, go to their graves like beds, fight for a plot... which is not tomb enough... How stand I then, that have a father kill'd, a mother stain'd... and let all sleep?

panels.prompt: extreme close-up of the prince's wind-whipped face against the grey sky, jaw set, eyes no longer sleepless but burning

dialogue.speaker: 哈姆雷特
dialogue.text: 啊，從這一刻起——讓我的思想只染血色，不然就一文不值！
dialogue.en: O, from this time forth, my thoughts be bloody, or be nothing worth!

quote.text: 讓我的思想只染血色，不然就一文不值
quote.en: My thoughts be bloody, or be nothing worth!

panels.prompt: a lone dark ship under sail on a vast black night sea, cold moonlight on the water, tiny lit portholes, framed like a woodcut with heavy black borders

dialogue.speaker: 旁白
dialogue.text: 船向英格蘭去。船上載著兩個同學、一封要他項上人頭的信——和一個已經下定決心的王子。
dialogue.en: The ship sails for England, carrying two schoolfellows, a letter that asks for his head — and a prince whose mind is made up at last.
